entries.german:
König Wenzel II gibt dem Stifte Hohenfurt für die Dörfer Strodenitz, Malschitz und Záboř acht andere Dörfer, worunter Stričitz, nebst der dasigen Kirche, und einen Theil des Waldes bei Dobschitz.

Nos Wencezlaus dei gratia rex Boemie dux Cracouie et Sandomerie marchioque Morauie harum serie notum esse uolumus tam presentibus quam futuris, quod felicis memorie dominus Otakarus illustris rex Boemie karissimus pater noster villam forensem dictam Zdradonicz circa ciuitatem nostram Budiwoyz necnon Plawen Malshiez et Zaborsi ad monasterium in Altovado Cisterciensis ordinis pertinentes accepit, quarum tres videlicet Zdradonicz Malschicz et Zaborsi dicte ciuitati adiunxit, pro quibus quatuor villis dictus pater noster villas dictas Nencitz Bellela Craschan et Tupes quondam Zuatumiri militis de Nemcicz in commutacionem prefato monasterio assignauit. Cumque per heredes dicti militis, quod eedem ville videlicet Nemchicz Bellela Craschän et Tupes ad eos racionabiliter pertinerent, nobis facta fuerit plena fides, eas restituendas duximus heredibus memoratis. Volentes itaque monasterium ipsum indempne super commutatione predicta seruare, villam predictam Plawen prefato monasterio restituimus et pro dictis tribus villis Zdradonicz Malshicz et Zaborsi villas nostras dictas Strishicz cum ecclesia in ea sita Borach Zaborsi Badiczi Holaschawicz Shemil Dubshicz Lupanawicz et partem silue Chraski usque ad metas inter bona monasterii Sancte Corone ac Henrici de Rosemberch et Johannis de Monte Michaelis, cum pratis pascuis agris cultis et incultis aquis et aquarum desursibus piscationibus et uenationibus ac iuribus omnibus racionibus et pertinenciis villarum ipsarum dicto monasterio de Altovado in cummutacionem damus tradimus et etiam assignamus, per abbatem et conuentum ipsius monasterii de Altovado commutationis titulo in perpetuum possidendas. In cuius rei testimonium presentes litteras fieri et sigillorum nostrorum munimine iussimus communiri. Datum Prage per manus magistri Petri prothonotarii nostri Pragensis Wratislauiensis et Wissegradensis ecclesiarum canonici. Anno domini millesimo ducentesimo nonagesimo secundo V o Nonas Julii. Indictionis quinte.

Siegel: Beschädigtes Siegel wie in XXXVIII.
entries.english: We, Wenceslaus, by the grace of God King of Bohemia, Duke of Cracow and Sandomierz, and Margrave of Moravia, make known to all present and future people that our father, the illustrious King Ottokar of blessed memory, took from the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt the market town of Zdradonicz near our city of Budweis, as well as Plawen, Malschitz, and Záboř, which belonged to the monastery. He incorporated three of these—Zdradonicz, Malschitz, and Záboř—into that city. In exchange for the four villages, our father assigned to the monastery the villages of Nencitz, Bellela, Craschan, and Tupes, formerly belonging to Zuatimir von Nemcicz, Ritter. Since the heirs of that knight have fully proved to us that these villages—Nemcicz, Bellela, Craschan, and Tupes—rightfully belong to them, we have judged that they must be restored to those heirs. Therefore, wishing to keep the monastery unharmed by the exchange, we restore Plawen to it and, in exchange for the three villages Zdradonicz, Malschitz, and Záboř, give, transfer, and assign to the monastery at Hohenfurt our villages Stričitz, with the church situated there, Borach, Záboř, Badiczi, Holaschawicz, Shemil, Dobschitz, and Lupanawicz, together with part of the Chraski forest up to the boundary between the lands of the monastery of Saint Corona and those of Heinrich von Rosenberg and Johann von Monte Michaelis. We grant these with meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated fields, waters and watercourses, fishing, hunting, all rights, claims, and appurtenances, for the abbot and convent at Hohenfurt to possess in perpetuity by title of exchange. To confirm this, we ordered this charter made and secured with our seals. Given at Prague by the hand of our protonotary Master Peter, canon of the churches of Prague, Wrocław, and Vyšehrad, on 3 July 1292, in the fifth indiction. The damaged seal is like that described in no. XXXVIII.
